concept.title: Introduction
concept.abstract: This section explains how the Markdown-to-DITA converter interprets Markdown package structures, page structures, metadata, headings, and content elements to generate DITA maps and topics. It covers package organization, folder hierarchies, metadata, mandatory and optional Markdown constructs, and conversion behaviors. The AI Agent learns how Markdown structure influences DITA map generation, topic classification, metadata mapping, content transformation, and the identification of structural issues that may affect conversion quality.

conbody.p: The Markdown-to-DITA converter reads the semantic structure of a Markdown package. The converter uses Markdown syntax, folder structure, metadata, and heading hierarchies to generate DITA maps, DITA topics, topic relationships, and semantic topic body elements.

When Markdown content is authored correctly, the converter can:
Create the root DITA map from the root index.md file and folder hierarchy.
Convert each Markdown file into DITA topics and establish parent-child relationships between topics.
Use metadata and Heading 1 (#) elements to create DITA map titles and topic titles.
Use the folder names to create DITA map and topic IDs.
Split the subsequent headings like heading 2 (##) through heading 3 (###) into separate DITA topics.
Preserve the topic sequence based on folder structure, index files, and heading levels.
Classify topics as concept, task, reference, troubleshooting, or glossary topics.
Convert paragraphs, lists, tables, images, hyperlinks, admonitions, and code blocks into valid DITA elements.
Generate or refine metadata such as short descriptions, authors, keywords, and index terms where supported.
Detect structural inconsistencies such as missing metadata, missing short descriptions, invalid links, duplicate IDs, orphan topics, improper nesting, or unsupported Markdown constructs that may require manual review.
